findings.description: The authoritative package_scope check in result_validator validates files_modified against package_def['scope'], but relies on the files_modified list as self-reported in the worker payload rather than verifying against the actual git commit diff. An untrusted worker modifying out-of-scope files could evade detection by omitting them from files_modified. As documented in design.md (D2), comparing files_modified against the commit diff is an explicit non-goal of this change, so this is acceptable.
findings.resolution: Accept; tracked as an explicit proposal non-goal in design.md.

findings.description: In validate_commit_resolves (validate_work_result.py), git is extracted via data.get('git') or {}. If data['git'] is a truthy non-dict (such as a string or integer), git.get('head') raises an unhandled AttributeError. At the acceptance decision point in accept_package_result, AttributeError is caught and safely converted to a refusal, ensuring fail-closed behavior. In standalone CLI usage, this results in an unhandled exception rather than structured check failure output.
findings.resolution: Accept; accept_package_result catches AttributeError and fail-closed refusal is preserved. A defensive isinstance check on data.get('git') could be added in a future pass.
